rules.missing_data: TODO: the protocol does not specify a threshold or method for handling missing outcome or covariate data. Propose complete-case analysis as the default for this pilot (n=100), with a pre-specified sensitivity analysis (e.g., best-case/worst-case for the primary outcome) triggered if missingness on the primary outcome exceeds 5%; multiple imputation may be considered for secondary continuous/ordinal outcomes if missingness is moderate and plausibly missing at random. rules.multiplicity: Only one confirmatory primary endpoint (P1, delivery-room intubation) exists, so no multiplicity correction is required for it. All secondary (S1-S3) and exploratory (E1-E2) analyses are supportive/hypothesis-generating, reported with point estimates and 95% CIs without adjustment for multiplicity, and are not used to claim confirmatory significance. rules.missing_data: TODO: the protocol does not state a missing-data threshold or handling rule. Proposed default: the primary analysis is complete-case, restricted to patients with an ascertainable 30-day outcome (per the estimand's own exclusion of patients with no ascertainable outcome); a pre-specified threshold (e.g., complete-case analysis if missingness on a given variable is under 5%, otherwise multiple imputation under a missing-at-random assumption with the pattern and proportion of missingness reported) needs to be fixed before analysis begins. Last observation carried forward is not used under any circumstance.
rules.multiplicity: TODO: the protocol does not pre-specify a multiplicity strategy. Proposed: P1 (30-day mortality) is the single confirmatory analysis at two-sided alpha 0.05, requiring no correction. S1-S3 secondary analyses are supportive and interpreted descriptively; if any secondary finding is later to be claimed as confirmatory, a Holm-Bonferroni correction within its own family (e.g., across the individual resistance phenotypes in S1) must be pre-specified. E1 is exploratory/hypothesis-generating and is not corrected for multiplicity; its estimates are reported for hypothesis generation only.

subgroups.how_tested: TODO: the sample-size justification references 'permitting subgroup analyses' without naming any subgroup, hypothesis, or target. If a subgroup analysis is intended (for example by age band, presentation severity, or source of infection), it must be pre-specified before analysis and tested via an interaction term (exposure group × subgroup) in the relevant regression model, never by comparing within-subgroup p-values against each other.
